title: MARPOL Annex I reg. 34.1.5 was taught as a single universal 1/30,000 at all seven candidate-facing sites in QB3_F, with 1/15,000 absent from the entire corpus
candidate_claim: Founder/GPT Tranche-3 independent review, finding F-4. An exhaustive corpus sweep found '1/30,000' at exactly seven candidate-facing positive teaching occurrences - QB3_F#q3 x5 and QB3_F#q11 x2 - and '1/15,000' at ZERO occurrences corpus-wide. Reg. 34.1.5 sets the total-quantity limit by the tanker's delivery date and has two limbs.
candidate_verdict: UPHELD, AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS READ RATHER THAN THE BRIEF'S STATEMENT OF THE RULE COPIED. ONE CORRECTION TO THE REPORTED SITE MAP, recorded rather than quietly absorbed: the attribution 'QB3_F#q11 x2' is not two sites in q11. Mapping every occurrence to its owning card by DOCUMENT POSITION - never by proximity - shows q11 owns ONE of them, and the seventh lives at line 873 in the page's 'Rapid Recall' cheat-grid card titled 'Annex I Reg 34 Cargo Discharge', which is OUTSIDE every q-card in the file. That matters twice over: it is fully candidate-facing and had to be corrected, and it can carry NO card digest, so it is asserted on CONTENT by this record's validator instead of by a pin. Counting seven and finding seven is not the same as knowing where they are.

authority.instrument: Resolution MEPC.117(52), Revised MARPOL Annex I, adopted 15 October 2004. Held at F:/RulesApp-Local-Input/true-source/03-imo-instruments/MARPOL-Annex-I/_base-and-amendments/MEPC.117(52).pdf, sha256 4921809d082be9cca96360ac9858a493bd5bf9238360d520f284854325d3356a, 105 pages. Registered SRC-MARPOL-ANNEXI-MEPC117-52, hash-pinned by this pass. Regulation 34 read in full from pages 58-59.
authority.operative_text_reg_34_1_5: '.5 the total quantity of oil discharged into the sea does not exceed for tankers delivered on or before 31 December 1979, as defined in regulation 1.28.1, 1/15,000 of the total quantity of the particular cargo of which the residue formed a part, and for tankers delivered after 31 December 1979, as defined in regulation 1.28.2, 1/30,000 of the total quantity of the particular cargo of which the residue formed a part'
authority.currency: The four later Annex I amendments held beside the base instrument - MEPC.187(59), MEPC.276(70), MEPC.314(74) and MEPC.359(79) - were each searched in full text for 'regulation 34'. ZERO hits in all four. Bounded deliberately: this establishes that no HELD amendment touches reg. 34, not that none exists anywhere, and the registry row's revalidation trigger is unchanged.
why_the_old_wording_was_wrong: It is wrong by a FACTOR OF TWO for every pre-1980-delivered tanker, in the conservative-sounding direction, which is the direction a candidate will not question.

The corpus contained no counter-example anywhere: '1/15,000' returned zero hits across all 86 files, so a candidate revising the whole bank could never have met the other limb. That is what makes this a propagation defect and not seven independent slips.

The 15-second and Key Numbers layers had reduced a two-limb conditional rule to a single number. The brief permits a compact split there, and that is what is used - but the 31 December 1979 boundary is stated exactly in every one of the seven forms, and no form omits a limb.

cards.supersession_note: NO SUPERSESSION ANCESTRY. Every batch and correction manifest on disk was scanned for a card record naming QB3_F.html#q3; there is none. The card has never been owned by a governed record, so digest resolution here is the ordinary pin == live comparison and no chain machinery engages.
changed_propositions: 15-second answer: 'at <=30 L/NM and <=1/30,000 of cargo total' -> the delivery-date limit with both limbs and both dates, compact form.

60-second answer: 'total quantity not exceeding 1/30,000 of the cargo' -> the full two-limb sentence in the instrument's own terms ('of the total quantity of the particular cargo of which the residue formed a part').

Body conditions list: the single-number bullet replaced by a nested two-limb bullet citing reg. 1.28.1 and reg. 1.28.2, closing with an explicit statement that there is no single universal fraction and that quoting 1/30,000 alone is wrong for every pre-1980 tanker.
Key Numbers: the single fraction replaced by the compact split.
Deep-dive Numbers & Regulations: the single fraction replaced by the compact split with the clause number and the words 'two limbs, never one number'.
deliberately_unchanged: Every other reg. 34.1 criterion - outside a special area, en route, more than 50 nautical miles from nearest land, 30 litres per nautical mile instantaneous rate, ODMCS and slop tank in operation. All were read against pages 58-59 and all are correct; the brief expressly directed that they not be altered.
The reg. 15 / 15 ppm machinery-space contrast, which is correct and is the card's other teaching point.

propagation.scope_pass: grep -o over all 86 files for '1/30,000|1/30000|1/15,000|30,000 of the total'. BEFORE: seven '1/30,000' (QB3_F only) and zero '1/15,000' anywhere. AFTER: seven and seven, in the same file, each 1/30,000 paired with its 1/15,000 limb. No other file in the corpus mentions the reg. 34 total-quantity fraction at all, so the propagation is complete and provably so - the completeness claim rests on the corpus-wide count being zero elsewhere, not on inspection of QB3_F alone.
propagation.revision_layer: QB3_F has no separate cheat-sheet file. Its revision surface is the in-page 'Rapid Recall' grid, which IS corrected here as an artefact.
